title: Pan-Fried Salmon with Herbs and Capers
subtitle: Crispy-skinned salmon with lemon, thyme, and capers
excerpt: Skin-on salmon fillets pan-fried until the skin is crisp, finished with garlic, capers, lemon, and parsley. This is a 15-minute dinner that never needs improving.
sourceNotes: Pan-fried salmon with a simple herb and caper butter is a staple of British and French home cooking. Salmon has been central to British coastal cuisine for centuries, and the combination of capers, lemon, and fresh herbs with pan-fried fish draws on the classic beurre meuniere tradition of French cookery.

content.text: Start the salmon skin-side down and leave it alone. Pressing it flat in the pan and not moving it for the first 3 to 4 minutes is what gets the skin truly crisp rather than soft and pale.
Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon fillets skin-side down. Press each fillet down gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds. Do not move them. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the skin is crisp and the salmon is cooked two-thirds of the way up the fillet.

Flip the fillets. Add the garlic, thyme sprigs, and capers to the pan. Cook for 2 to 3 more minutes until the salmon is just cooked through. The flesh should flake easily but still be slightly translucent in the centre.
Remove the salmon and thyme sprigs. Add the lemon juice and parsley to the pan juices and stir briefly. Spoon over the salmon and serve with lemon wedges.

items.symptom: Skin is sticking to the pan
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or fish was moved too soon
items.fix: Use a hot pan and do not move the fillet until the skin releases on its own.

items.cause: Left in the pan too long after flipping
items.fix: Flip once and check after 2 minutes. Remove while still slightly pink inside.

items.symptom: Skin is soft rather than crisp
items.cause: Salmon was wet or pan too cool
items.fix: Pat skin dry before cooking and make sure the oil is hot before adding fish.
